dataset: dHCP fetal atlas GW21-GW36 (parcellations_scaled), cortical GM included
label_legend_note: Point this at 'info/dhcp-atlas-summary-info-19-labels.csv' inside your copy of the dHCP atlas download (an equivalent ITK-SnAP .txt sits beside it). Left empty here because its location depends on where you unpacked the atlas.
label_selection_note: Cerebrum INCLUDING cortical GM, so the rendered boundary is the pial surface. Kept: 3,4 Cortical GM L/R; 5,6 Fetal WM L/R; 7,8 Lateral Ventricle L/R; 9 Cavum septum pellucidum; 14,15 Basal Ganglia L/R; 16,17 Thalamus L/R; 18 Third Ventricle. Dropped: 1,2 eCSF (it would fill the sulci and erase the gyrification signal); 10 Brainstem; 11,12 Cerebellum; 13 Vermis; 19 Fourth Ventricle.
companion_note: Companion to area_band_config_dhcp_atlas.example.json, which excludes 3,4 and therefore measures the white-matter/subplate boundary - the selection that reproduces what the fetal_surface runs measured. This config measures the pial boundary instead. Without cortex the sulcal invaginations of the WM boundary reach deeper than the brain's actual surface, which is what makes the sulci look over-concave from about GW30 on. The two selections are NOT comparable on area, perimeter or LGI (GW36 coronal: LGI 2.20 without cortex vs 1.70 with, area +37 percent, and the gap widens with gestational age). Keep them in separate output roots and never mix them in one workbook.
paths_note: batch_dir/batch_out are machine-specific and deliberately empty here. Copy this file to configs/area_band_config_dhcp_atlas_cortex.json (gitignored) and fill them in, or pass --batch-dir/--batch-out on the command line. Use a batch_out separate from the no-cortex run.
